chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
The destitute is the Messenger of Allah. Whoever denies him denies Allah, and whoever gives him gives Allah.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of giving to the poor in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this famous saying from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elevates the status of the destitute by identifying them as 'messengers' of Allah, thereby transforming the act of charity from a social duty into a direct transaction with the Divine. This concept underscores the Shia emphasis on the spiritual merit of recognizing the poor as carriers of Allah's message, where giving to them is akin to giving to Allah Himself, and withholding is a form of divine denial.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 304. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
The destitute is the Messenger of Allāh. Whoever denies him denies Allāh and whoever gives him gives Allāh.
